AttachmentFromUrlRequest.description:
Request body for POST /api/v1/attachments/from-url.

Fetches a remote URL server-side, validates the bytes against the
same MIME / size rules as POST /upload, stores them in our private
GCS bucket, and returns an attachment ID. Per-tenant URL dedup: the
same `url` will return the existing attachment without re-fetching.

filename.description: Optional override for the stored filename. If omitted, the filename is derived from the URL path, falling back to a UUID-based name.
filename.title: Filename

url.description: Public http(s) URL to fetch. file://, gopher://, etc. are rejected. Hostnames resolving to private/loopback/link-local IPs are blocked (SSRF protection).
url.title: Url

download_url.description: Signed GCS URL for download (alias for url)
download_url.title: Download Url

is_inline.description: Whether this is an inline attachment

url.description: Signed GCS URL for download (frontend uses this)
url.title: Url

attachment_id.description: Alias of `id` — preferred name for new callers. Persist this rather than the URL so future URL-form changes are transparent.
attachment_id.title: Attachment Id

download_url.description: Authenticated proxy URL for downloading the attachment. Same-origin path (e.g. `/api/v1/attachments/{id}/download`) the browser fetches with the user's session cookie. The underlying GCS bucket is private; this is NOT a public URL. Use this for in-app render / agent UI / bot flows.
download_url.title: Download Url

public_url.description: Absolute, **unauthenticated** public URL for the attachment (e.g. `https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/attachments/public/{tenant_id}/{attachment_id}/{filename}`). Use this only for outbound contexts where an external service must `GET` the bytes — WhatsApp template `image.link` (Meta caches on first send), third-party webhook payloads, etc. The URL acts as a capability: anyone who has it can fetch the bytes. Don't put it in places that don't need it.
public_url.title: Public Url

url.title: Url

CarouselCardRequest.description:
A single carousel card within a CAROUSEL component.

A card mirrors a mini-template: its ``components`` list holds exactly one
HEADER (format IMAGE or VIDEO), exactly one BODY, and an optional BUTTONS
component. This is shape-only — structural rules (card count, header
format, cross-card consistency) are enforced at the route/service layer.

Security hardening (API DoS): the mutual recursion between this model and
``TemplateComponentRequest`` (``components`` -> ``cards`` -> ``components``)
is capped here fail-closed. An inner card component may ONLY be
HEADER/BODY/BUTTONS — never a nested CAROUSEL, and never carry its own
``cards`` — and each BODY is length-bounded. This runs as a ``mode="before"``
validator so a hostile deeply-nested payload is rejected BEFORE Pydantic
recurses into (and fully parses) the inner components.

components.description: The card's components: one IMAGE/VIDEO HEADER, one BODY, and an optional BUTTONS component (<=2 buttons).
components.title: Components

CarouselCardRequest.title: CarouselCardRequest

ChannelChainEntry.description:
One entry in a Send node's ``channel_chain``.

The wire shape historically was ``list[str]`` — each item a channel
type ("whatsapp", "email", ...). It now widens to accept EITHER a
bare string OR an object pinning a specific Channel row::

    # Legacy bare-string form (still supported):
    ["whatsapp", "email"]

    # New object form — pin to a specific WhatsApp / Messenger page:
    [
      {"channel_type": "whatsapp", "channel_id": "<uuid>"},
      {"channel_type": "email"},  # channel_id null → tenant-default
    ]

Bare strings are normalized to ``ChannelChainEntry(channel_type=s,
channel_id=None)`` via ``normalize_channel_chain`` so service-layer
code (``send_node.py``, ``observability``, etc.) sees a single shape.

ChannelResponse.description:
Schema for channel response.

SECURITY: The 'config' field is intentionally excluded. It contains
API tokens, secrets, and credentials that must NEVER be returned via API.
Use 'identifier' for display purposes (phone number, bot username, page ID).

For WhatsApp channels:
- ``identifier`` returns a purely numeric phone number (no '+' or spaces)
- ``phone_number_formatted`` returns the human-readable formatted number

For RCS channels, three NON-SECRET columns are surfaced so the channel UI
can render the agent identity and the launch lifecycle straight off the
``GET /channels`` row. The two secret RCS columns
(``rcs_service_account_json`` -- one key that can send as ANY of our
agents -- and ``rcs_client_token``) are deliberately absent and MUST NEVER
be added here or to any other read schema.

``rcs_message_traffic_type`` is the ONE ``config`` key this schema exposes,
and it arrives via the ``Channel.rcs_message_traffic_type`` **property** --
not by relaxing the config exclusion. Do not "simplify" that into returning
``config`` (or a filtered copy of it): the exclusion above is the reason a
rotated ``access_token`` has never come back out of this endpoint, and a
passthrough is how the next new secret key would.

activation_status.description: ES/Coexistence activation lifecycle. `null` = ACTIVE (legacy / healthy channels). `AVAILABLE` = the channel row exists but setup is not complete (see `setup_pending_reason`); such a channel is `is_active=false` and MUST NOT be rendered as connected.
activation_status.title: Activation Status

avatar_url.description: Profile picture of the connected account on this channel (Facebook Page / Instagram account). Null when unavailable or not captured for this channel type. Meta CDN URLs expire — do not persist client-side.
avatar_url.title: Avatar Url

rcs_agent_id.description: [RCS] Google RBM agent id, stored BARE (no '@rbm.goog' suffix). Normalisation happens on write via a model @validates hook.
rcs_agent_id.title: Rcs Agent Id

rcs_launch_state.description: [RCS] Free-form brand-verification + per-carrier launch status. Absent/empty means NOTHING is launched (fail closed): pre-launch an agent can only reach allowlisted tester devices.
rcs_launch_state.title: Rcs Launch State

rcs_message_traffic_type.description: [RCS] The channel's DEFAULT `messageTrafficType` (`AUTHENTICATION` | `TRANSACTION` | `PROMOTION` | `SERVICEREQUEST` | `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT`), or `null` when none is set. A German regulatory declaration about the nature of the message (UWG / telecoms), NOT a billing tier and not a delivery-speed setting. `null` means unset -- the adapter then falls back to `SERVICEREQUEST` -- and is what an archived channel reads, since this value is deliberately not preserved across archiving. Returned canonicalised, i.e. exactly the value that will be sent to Google; a stored value outside the five enum values reads as `null` because that is what the adapter will make of it. Set it with `PUT /channels/{id}/rcs/credentials`.
rcs_message_traffic_type.title: Rcs Message Traffic Type

rcs_pricing_mode.description: [RCS] How this RCS agent is billed (read-only; set by SendSeven): `per_message` = each message is billed and counts towards your messages; `mau` = billed once per monthly active recipient, and its messages do NOT count as messages sent. `null` on every non-RCS channel.
rcs_pricing_mode.title: Rcs Pricing Mode

setup_pending_reason.description: Non-null when the channel row exists but setup is INCOMPLETE and needs customer action. `coexistence_setup_incomplete` = the WhatsApp number must finish Coexistence setup on the phone (keep it active on the WhatsApp Business App, re-run connect, and complete Meta's dialog incl. the QR scan + on-handset confirmation). `null` for every fully-set-up channel. A channel with this set is NOT connected and must not render as such.

auto_translate_messages.description: Per-flow opt-in for runtime LLM translation of outbound Send-node messages into the contact's preferred language.

default_channel_chain.description: Flow-level channel fallback chain — May 2026 this is the SINGLE source of truth for channel order (per-node ``channel_chain`` has been removed; node configs only carry content). Bare channel-type strings (``["whatsapp", "live_chat"]``) OR ``{channel_type, channel_id?}`` objects pinning a specific Channel row. When omitted / NULL on create, the server seeds from the tenant's active channels in a sensible order. A flow with any send/choice/collect_input node MUST have a non-empty chain to validate.
default_channel_chain.title: Default Channel Chain

default_language.description: Per-flow fallback language used by the runtime when a contact has no resolvable locale. Typically set by the frontend to the operator's current UI language at create time. Backend defaults to ``'en'`` (DB server_default) if omitted. Must be one of the curated ~40 ``SUPPORTED_TRANSLATION_LOCALES``.
default_language.title: Default Language

definition.description: The full flow graph: ``trigger`` + ``nodes[]`` + ``edges[]`` + ``entry_node_id``. See ``fl01_create_flows.py`` migration docstring for the locked JSON shape. Hard-capped at 256 KB JSON-encoded; validated against the structural rules in ``FlowDefinitionValidator``.
definition.title: Definition

exclusive.description: When True, while a run of this entry-triggered flow is actively running on a conversation, NO other entry-triggered flow may start on that conversation (background manual/api/schedule flows are exempt). Default False preserves today's fire-all behaviour.
exclusive.title: Exclusive

language_detection_strategy.description: How this flow's runs resolve the language they speak to a contact. ``cascade`` (the default) resolves per run via the fallback chain (contact locale → inferred channel locale → ``default_language``). ``fixed`` always speaks ``default_language``, skipping the cascade. OMIT / ``null`` to keep the default — NULL is stored and treated as ``cascade`` by the runtime, so existing flows are unaffected. Any value other than ``cascade`` / ``fixed`` is rejected with 422.
language_detection_strategy.title: Language Detection Strategy

manually_triggerable.description: When True, the flow appears in the operator's manual-start picker and accepts ``POST /flows/{id}/runs`` requests. Automatically forced True when the trigger kind is ``manual``.
manually_triggerable.title: Manually Triggerable

priority.description: Trigger-arbitration priority among INBOUND-EVENT-triggered (entry) flows. LOWER = higher priority (evaluated FIRST). When multiple entry flows match the same inbound event they start in ascending-priority order. Default 0. Background flows (manual/api_event/schedule) ignore this field.
priority.title: Priority

re_entry_policy.description: How to behave when the same contact is triggered again while a run is already in flight. MVP only enforces ``block`` (ignore the new trigger). ``restart`` and ``parallel`` are scaffolded for Phase 3 UX.
re_entry_policy.title: Re Entry Policy

stop_on_agent_reply.description: When True (the default), the flow engine terminates any active run for the contact + conversation the moment a human agent sends an outbound message. Bot replies and flow-Send messages do NOT trip the hook — only operator-authored outbound messages do. Set to False for long-running drips whose cadence should be independent of agent activity.
stop_on_agent_reply.title: Stop On Agent Reply

stop_on_conversation_closed.description: When True (the default), the flow engine terminates any active run scoped to the conversation the moment that conversation is closed. Only runs whose recorded ``context.conversation_id`` matches the closed conversation are canceled — flows without a recorded conversation are left untouched. Set to False for long-running re-engagement drips that intentionally outlive the original conversation.
stop_on_conversation_closed.title: Stop On Conversation Closed

channel_id.description: Pinned channel UUID — REQUIRED for chat-app channel types (whatsapp, telegram, sms, messenger, instagram, rcs). The channel IS the sender for these. Must be NULL for ``channel_type=email`` (use ``email_mailbox_id`` instead).
channel_id.title: Channel Id

email_mailbox_id.description: Pinned EmailMailbox UUID — REQUIRED for ``channel_type=email``. The mailbox is the sender (controls the From: address). Must be NULL for chat-app channel types.
email_mailbox_id.title: Email Mailbox Id

next_evaluation_at.description: For `segment_blast`: the dispatch time. For other kinds the evaluator manages this cursor — leaving it NULL is fine.
next_evaluation_at.title: Next Evaluation At

payload.description: Free-form JSON payload. Same per-channel rules as ``scheduled_sends.payload``: WhatsApp REQUIRES ``{template_id, variables}``; email accepts EITHER free-text (``{subject, text|html}``) OR templated (``{template_id, variables?}``) — mutually exclusive; SMS/Telegram/Messenger/Instagram/RCS must NOT carry ``template_id`` but MAY carry ``attachments`` (a list of ≤20 attachment UUIDs owned by your workspace). Hard-capped at 64 KB.
payload.title: Payload

recurrence_rule.description: iCalendar RRULE string. Required for `recurring_cron`; must be NULL for `birthday` and `segment_blast`.
recurrence_rule.title: Recurrence Rule

segment_filter.description:
Audience selector. Two accepted shapes:
  * NEW: ``{"match_op": "any"|"all", "rules": [{"kind": "tag"|"list"|"language", "op": ..., "values": [...]}]}``
  * LEGACY: ``{"tags": [...], "tags_op": "any"|"all"}`` (normalized by the engine).
NULL for `birthday` (audience is implicit).
segment_filter.title: Segment Filter

time_of_day_local.description: Local clock time as "HH:MM" or "HH:MM:SS". Required for `birthday` rules. Optional for `recurring_cron` (the RRULE controls timing). Ignored for `segment_blast`.
time_of_day_local.title: Time Of Day Local

timezone.description: IANA tz name (e.g. ``Europe/Berlin``). NULL semantics: birthday → contact-local TZ, recurring_cron/segment_blast → UTC.
timezone.title: Timezone

channel_id.description: Pinned channel UUID — REQUIRED for chat-app channel types (whatsapp, telegram, sms, messenger, instagram, rcs). Each chat-app channel IS the sender (for RCS: the RBM agent). Leave NULL only for ``channel_type=email`` (use ``email_mailbox_id`` instead).
channel_id.title: Channel Id

contact_id.description: Contact UUID on the tenant's shard
contact_id.title: Contact Id

email_mailbox_id.description: Pinned EmailMailbox UUID — REQUIRED for ``channel_type=email``. The mailbox is the sender (controls the From: address and the underlying provider/integration). Must be NULL for chat-app channel types (use ``channel_id`` instead).
email_mailbox_id.title: Email Mailbox Id

payload.description:
Free-form JSON payload. Per-channel rules:
  - WhatsApp: REQUIRES ``{template_id, variables}`` — free text is rejected because the 24h messaging window cannot be guaranteed at schedule time.
  - Email: EITHER ``{subject, text|html, include_signature?}`` (free-text) OR ``{template_id, variables?}`` (references an EmailContent template). Mutually exclusive.
  - SMS / Telegram / Messenger / Instagram / RCS: rendered text payload (e.g. ``{"text": "..."}``), optionally with ``attachments`` — a list of attachment UUIDs (uploaded via ``POST /attachments/upload``) fanned out as one message per attachment at fire time. Max 20. Every id must belong to your workspace.
Hard-capped at 64 KB JSON-encoded.
payload.title: Payload

recurrence_rule.description: Optional iCalendar RRULE (e.g. ``FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9``). When set, the row stays in ``scheduled`` after firing and ``next_run_at`` advances per the rule. Capped at 255 chars.
recurrence_rule.title: Recurrence Rule

send_at.description: First-fire timestamp (timezone-aware UTC). Must be at least 1 minute in the future.
send_at.title: Send At

timezone.description: IANA timezone for recurrence interpretation (e.g. ``Europe/Berlin``). Defaults to UTC. Currently informational; recurrence math runs in UTC so this is preserved for display only.
timezone.title: Timezone

EmailContentCreate.description:
Schema for creating email content with variable system.

Supports two content types:
- **html** (default): Full MJML content with visual editor support
- **plain_text**: Plain text template with {{variable}} placeholders

The variable system supports 4 types of variables:
1. Template variables: Custom content (e.g., {{hero_title}}, {{cta_url}})
   - Filled via variable_values field or form mode
2. Contact variables: Auto-filled from contact data (e.g., {{contact.name}})
   - Replaced at send time with actual contact data
3. Company variables: Auto-filled from company data (e.g., {{company.name}})
   - Replaced at send time with company info
4. System variables: Auto-filled by platform (e.g., {{system.year}})
   - Replaced at send time with system values

Variable naming convention: lowercase_with_underscores
Examples: hero_title, contact.name (valid), heroTitle, hero-title (invalid)

FlowRunMessageResponse.description:
``MessageResponse`` variant for the flow-run transcript endpoint
(``GET /flows/{flow_id}/runs/{run_id}/messages``).

Flow Send-node messages are persisted BEFORE any conversation exists
(``messages.conversation_id`` was relaxed to NULL in ``fl06``; the
messages_in_worker backfill stitches them into the contact's first
inbound reply later). Test runs and runs that never got a reply keep
``conversation_id = NULL`` forever, which the public ``MessageResponse``
originally rejected (``conversation_id: str``) — Sentry BACKEND-8Y. The
base ``MessageResponse.conversation_id`` is now itself ``Optional[str]``
(campaign mirror messages hit the same case); this subclass keeps its
flow-specific field description and remains the endpoint's response model.

campaign.description: Campaign info when this message was sent via a campaign/newsletter

contact_info.description: Provider-echoed sender profile captured from the inbound channel webhook at receipt time (inbound message.received only; not a DB lookup). Fields vary by channel: WhatsApp {name, phone}, Telegram {name, username, profile_picture}, Messenger {name, profile_picture}, Instagram {name?, username, profile_picture}. NOTE: `phone` (WhatsApp-only) is deprecated — use `data.contact_method.value` for the authoritative DB-sourced identifier of the method actually used.
contact_info.title: Contact Info

content_format.description: How this message's body is formatted for the send pipeline: `markdown` (canonical markdown, rendered per-channel) or `plain` (human text, passed through untouched). Derived from `meta.content_format`; defaults to `plain` for every message that did not explicitly opt into markdown.
content_format.title: Content Format

conversation_id.description: Conversation the message belongs to. Null for flow messages that were sent before any conversation existed (e.g. test runs, or runs the contact never replied to).
conversation_id.title: Conversation Id

edited_at.description: When this message was last edited by the sender (real column on `messages`, stamped when an edit event is applied). Non-null is the ONLY signal that a message was edited — `text` is silently replaced in place, so without this a client cannot tell an edited message from an original one. Null for every message that was never edited (the overwhelming majority).
edited_at.title: Edited At

flow_name.description: Display name of the flow that sent this message. NOT stored on the message row — populated by the API layer via a single batch lookup against `flow_runs JOIN flows` and only set when `flow_run_id` is non-null.
flow_name.title: Flow Name

flow_run_id.description: FlowRun UUID — set when this message was sent by an automation flow. Frontends use this (together with `flow_name`) to render a 'Sent by flow' badge in the conversation timeline.
flow_run_id.title: Flow Run Id

flow_step_id.description: FlowRunStep UUID — identifies the specific Send-node step inside the flow that produced this message. Optional companion to `flow_run_id`.
flow_step_id.title: Flow Step Id

header_media_attachment_id.description: Durable attachment id for an interactive image/video header
header_media_attachment_id.title: Header Media Attachment Id

header_media_url.description: Resolved media URL for an interactive image/video header
header_media_url.title: Header Media Url

interactive.description: Interactive message content (WhatsApp-style Meta format) for messages with reply buttons or a list. Hydrated from `meta.interactive`. Null for non-interactive/legacy messages.

previous_text.description: Body this message had immediately BEFORE its most recent edit. Not stored on the message row — resolved by the API layer from the newest APPLIED `message_revisions` row in one batched lookup per page. Null means 'edited, but the superseded body is unknown': most edits arrive before/without the message they target, so the original body was often never captured. Clients must therefore treat null as valid and fall back to a plain non-interactive 'edited' marker instead of an edit-history UI.
previous_text.title: Previous Text

related_message_ids.description: IDs of the additional messages created by the same send request, in delivery order. Non-empty only when a send carried several attachments on a channel that delivers one attachment per message — the response body itself is the FIRST message (it holds the caption and `attachments[0]`), and each id here is a further message carrying the next attachment. Each has its own status and its own delivery webhooks, so poll them individually via `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}`. Empty array for every other message.
related_message_ids.title: Related Message Ids

reply_to_external_id.description: Platform message ID of quoted message
reply_to_external_id.title: Reply To External Id

revision_count.description: Number of edits that have actually been APPLIED to this message. Pending revisions (an edit whose target message we never resolved) are deliberately excluded — they describe no visible change to this row. 0 for un-edited messages; a value >1 tells the client the body was edited repeatedly, so `previous_text` is only the last step of a longer history.

InvitationRoleEnum.description:
Allowed invitation roles - maps to RBAC system roles.

There are exactly 7 system roles (migration 059, Jan 2026, consolidated the
original 10 and renamed them SCREAMING_SNAKE -> display case). The slugs below
map onto them in ``app/api/invitations.py::role_mapping``:

- OWNER            -> "Owner"          Full access to everything (*:*)
- ADMIN            -> "Admin"          Full access EXCEPT billing (zero billing scopes)
- SUPPORT_AGENT    -> "Support Agent"  Conversations, tickets, contacts, knowledge base
- MARKETING_AGENT  -> "Marketing"      Campaigns, email, lists, contacts
- VIEWER           -> "Viewer"         Read-only access to all resources
- BILLING_ADMIN    -> "Billing"        Billing management only
- DEVELOPER        -> "Developer"      API tokens, webhooks, technical settings

ANALYST, CONTENT_MANAGER and DESIGNER are RETIRED roles. They are kept in this
enum only so old pending invitations still resolve, and they fold onto a
surviving role (analyst/designer -> Viewer, content_manager -> Marketing).
Do NOT offer them in new UI or docs.

New integrations should pass ``role_id`` (an RBAC Role UUID from ``GET /roles``)
instead of a slug -- that path also supports tenant-created custom roles.

MessageCreate.description:
Schema for creating/sending a new message.

Supports 3 resolution modes:

**Mode 1: conversation_id only** (reply to existing conversation)
- Provide just `conversation_id` and `text`. The recipient (`to`) is automatically
  resolved from the conversation's contact method or last inbound message.
- Example: ``{"conversation_id": "...", "text": "Hello!"}``

**Mode 2: contact_method_id** (cleanest, resolves everything)
- Provide `contact_method_id` and `text`. The `to`, `channel_id`, and `contact_id`
  are all resolved from the contact method record.
- Example: ``{"contact_method_id": "...", "text": "Hello!"}``

**Mode 3: contact_id + optional to + channel_id** (explicit, auto-creates contact_method)
- Provide `contact_id` (and optionally `to` and `channel_id`). The conversation is
  auto-resolved from the contact. A contact_method is auto-created if one doesn't exist.
- Example: ``{"contact_id": "...", "to": "+49...", "text": "Hello!"}``

Fields:
- to: Recipient external ID (phone, telegram_id, etc.) - optional when conversation_id
  or contact_method_id is provided
- conversation_id: Optional, conversation to send in (auto-resolved if not provided)
- contact_method_id: Optional, cleanest way to send - resolves to, channel_id, and
  contact_id automatically
- contact_id: Optional, used to auto-resolve conversation when conversation_id is omitted
- channel_id: Optional, used when creating a new conversation or for ambiguous recipients
- message_type: Optional, defaults to "text"
- text: Message content
- attachments: Optional list of attachment IDs
- meta: Optional customer-defined metadata

examples.description: Send a text message to an existing conversation. The recipient is auto-resolved from the conversation's contact method.

value.text: Hello! Your order has been shipped.

examples.description: Send a message using a contact method ID. Everything (to, channel_id, contact_id) is resolved automatically.

value.text: Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow.

examples.description: Send a message to a contact. The conversation is auto-resolved and a contact_method is auto-created if needed.
Send a text message with explicit recipient to an existing conversation.

value.text: Hello! Your order has been shipped.

attachment_filenames.description: Optional per-message display-filename overrides for `attachments`, aligned positionally by index (entry N overrides the filename of `attachments[N]`). Controls the filename shown to the recipient — e.g. Meta's `filename` field on a WhatsApp document, so the user sees `Invoice-2026.pdf` instead of the stored object name. When omitted (or an entry is null/empty), the send path falls back to the original filename stored on the Attachment record (`attachments.filename`). If the list is shorter than `attachments`, only the leading attachments are overridden; extra entries beyond the number of attachments are ignored. Every entry now takes effect: on a channel that delivers one attachment per message, entry N is the filename of the message carrying `attachments[N]`.
attachment_filenames.title: Attachment Filenames

attachments.description:
Attachment IDs (UUIDs) returned from POST /api/v1/attachments/upload or POST /api/v1/attachments/from-url. Do NOT pass raw URLs here — fetch them via /attachments/from-url first to get an ID.

Accepts either an array or a single bare ID string (`"<uuid>"` is treated as `["<uuid>"]`). Whitespace is trimmed and empty entries are dropped.

On channels that can only carry ONE media object per message (WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger, Instagram, SMS/MMS, browser push, RCS) several attachments are delivered as several messages — one per attachment, with `text` used as the caption of the FIRST one. This response returns the first message; the additional ones are listed in `related_message_ids`. Email (MIME parts) and live chat deliver all attachments inside a single message.
attachments.title: Attachments

MessageResponse.description:
Schema for message response.

Unified message format for all channels with simplified from/to fields.
- platform: Channel type (whatsapp, telegram, etc.) at message level for filtering
- channel_id: Always represents "our side" (the business's channel)
- contact_id: Link to Contact for name lookup
- from: External ID (only set for inbound messages)
- to: External ID (only set for outbound messages)
- contact_info: Messenger-specific data (only for inbound)
- meta: Customer-defined arbitrary JSON

campaign.description: Campaign info when this message was sent via a campaign/newsletter

contact_info.description: Provider-echoed sender profile captured from the inbound channel webhook at receipt time (inbound message.received only; not a DB lookup). Fields vary by channel: WhatsApp {name, phone}, Telegram {name, username, profile_picture}, Messenger {name, profile_picture}, Instagram {name?, username, profile_picture}. NOTE: `phone` (WhatsApp-only) is deprecated — use `data.contact_method.value` for the authoritative DB-sourced identifier of the method actually used.
contact_info.title: Contact Info

content_format.description: How this message's body is formatted for the send pipeline: `markdown` (canonical markdown, rendered per-channel) or `plain` (human text, passed through untouched). Derived from `meta.content_format`; defaults to `plain` for every message that did not explicitly opt into markdown.
content_format.title: Content Format

conversation_id.description: Conversation the message belongs to. May be null for campaign and flow messages sent to a contact that has no conversation on that channel (campaigns never create conversations; flow messages are attached once the contact replies).
conversation_id.title: Conversation Id

edited_at.description: When this message was last edited by the sender (real column on `messages`, stamped when an edit event is applied). Non-null is the ONLY signal that a message was edited — `text` is silently replaced in place, so without this a client cannot tell an edited message from an original one. Null for every message that was never edited (the overwhelming majority).
edited_at.title: Edited At

flow_name.description: Display name of the flow that sent this message. NOT stored on the message row — populated by the API layer via a single batch lookup against `flow_runs JOIN flows` and only set when `flow_run_id` is non-null.
flow_name.title: Flow Name

flow_run_id.description: FlowRun UUID — set when this message was sent by an automation flow. Frontends use this (together with `flow_name`) to render a 'Sent by flow' badge in the conversation timeline.
flow_run_id.title: Flow Run Id

flow_step_id.description: FlowRunStep UUID — identifies the specific Send-node step inside the flow that produced this message. Optional companion to `flow_run_id`.
flow_step_id.title: Flow Step Id

header_media_attachment_id.description: Durable attachment id for an interactive image/video header
header_media_attachment_id.title: Header Media Attachment Id

header_media_url.description: Resolved media URL for an interactive image/video header
header_media_url.title: Header Media Url

interactive.description: Interactive message content (WhatsApp-style Meta format) for messages with reply buttons or a list. Hydrated from `meta.interactive`. Null for non-interactive/legacy messages.

previous_text.description: Body this message had immediately BEFORE its most recent edit. Not stored on the message row — resolved by the API layer from the newest APPLIED `message_revisions` row in one batched lookup per page. Null means 'edited, but the superseded body is unknown': most edits arrive before/without the message they target, so the original body was often never captured. Clients must therefore treat null as valid and fall back to a plain non-interactive 'edited' marker instead of an edit-history UI.
previous_text.title: Previous Text

related_message_ids.description: IDs of the additional messages created by the same send request, in delivery order. Non-empty only when a send carried several attachments on a channel that delivers one attachment per message — the response body itself is the FIRST message (it holds the caption and `attachments[0]`), and each id here is a further message carrying the next attachment. Each has its own status and its own delivery webhooks, so poll them individually via `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}`. Empty array for every other message.
related_message_ids.title: Related Message Ids

reply_to_external_id.description: Platform message ID of quoted message
reply_to_external_id.title: Reply To External Id

revision_count.description: Number of edits that have actually been APPLIED to this message. Pending revisions (an edit whose target message we never resolved) are deliberately excluded — they describe no visible change to this row. 0 for un-edited messages; a value >1 tells the client the body was edited repeatedly, so `previous_text` is only the last step of a longer history.
revision_count.title: Revision Count

OpenOrCreateConversationRequest.description:
Request to open an existing conversation or create a new one.

This is a simplified endpoint that does NOT send a message.
Use this when you want to navigate to a conversation and compose
messages using the normal chat UI.

For email channels, use `use_conversation_id` to specify which existing
thread to use instead of creating a new one.

**Two-phase API usage:**
1. First call `/conversations/check-existing` to see if open/closed conversations exist
2. Then call this endpoint with `action` to specify what to do:
   - `action="create_new"`: Always create a new conversation (fires webhook)
   - `action="reopen_existing"`: Reopen closed conversation (fires conversation.reopened webhook)
   - `action="auto"` (default): Backwards compatible behavior

contact_method_id.description: Optional. Bind the conversation to a SPECIFIC contact method (e.g. one of the contact's several email addresses / phone numbers) instead of resolving the recipient via the channel's primary method. Must belong to the same contact + tenant and be compatible with the channel's method type (a PHONE method is also accepted for a WhatsApp channel). For email the synthetic 'email_mailbox_<uuid>' / 'email_integration_<uuid>' channel_id is validated as an EMAIL method type. When a NEW conversation is created both contact_method_id and active_contact_method_id are set to this value; when an existing conversation is reused only active_contact_method_id is updated. When omitted, behavior is unchanged (recipient resolved via the channel's primary method).
contact_method_id.title: Contact Method Id

reopen_existing.description: DEPRECATED: Use action='reopen_existing' instead. If True and a closed conversation exists, reopen it. If False, always create new.
reopen_existing.title: Reopen Existing

use_conversation_id.description: For email: specify an existing conversation ID to use instead of creating new. This allows continuing an existing email thread.

PrivateReplyQuickReply.description:
One quick reply chip in a private reply. Supported on Facebook
Messenger and Instagram alike.

a button template is just the attachment the chips accompany.

RcsCapabilityResponse.description:
Per-recipient reachability for THIS agent.

``reachable: false`` is an ANSWER, not an error. RBM returns 404 for every
kind of unreachable — no RCS on the device, RCS switched off, a carrier the
agent is not launched on, or a tester who has not accepted the invite yet —
and it cannot tell them apart. So the endpoint returns 200 with
``reachable: false`` and a coarse ``reason``; inventing a specific cause
would be a guess presented as a fact.

reason.title: Reason

tester_status.title: Tester Status

RcsCapabilityResponse.title: RcsCapabilityResponse

RcsContent.description:
RCS for Business (Google RBM) campaign content.

Note what is NOT here: RBM has no template approval and no 24-hour
re-engagement window, so none of the WhatsApp template fields transfer —
there is no template id/name/language/category and no variable_mapping.
Content is composed freely.

``message_traffic_type`` is also deliberately absent. It is a German carrier
/regulatory declaration about the nature of the message (UWG §7), and the
campaigns worker always declares ``PROMOTION`` for Reach traffic; a
per-campaign override would let marketing be declared as transactional.

Bounds are enforced by ``RcsAdapter`` rather than repeated here, so this
schema cannot drift from the platform: text is auto-split at 3072 chars, the
whole AgentMessage is capped at 250 KB, suggestions at 11 per message but 4
per card with 25-char labels and 2048-char postbackData, and carousels must
hold 2–10 cards.

RecrawlRequest.description:
Request model for re-crawling a previously crawled domain.

Supports two modes:
- "existing_pages": Re-crawl the exact URLs from previous crawl history (faster, predictable)
- "full_rescan": Re-discover pages via sitemap/BFS from scratch (finds new pages, more thorough)

Both modes use non-destructive crawl-then-reconcile: existing documents are updated in-place,
new documents are created, and orphaned documents (not touched by this crawl) are removed
only after the crawl completes successfully.

clear_existing.description: Hard reset. When True, the existing documents for this domain (and their RAG corpus files) are deleted BEFORE the re-crawl runs, then pages are re-discovered and re-imported from scratch. When False (default), the re-crawl is non-destructive: existing documents are updated in-place and orphaned documents are cleaned up only after a successful crawl (crawl-then-reconcile).
clear_existing.title: Clear Existing

history_id.description: ID of the crawl history record to use for re-crawling
history_id.title: History Id

mode.description: Recrawl mode. Defaults to 'full_rescan', which re-discovers pages from scratch via sitemap/BFS and picks up newly added pages. 'existing_pages' re-crawls only the URLs stored from the previous crawl.
mode.title: Mode

page_limit.description: Maximum pages to crawl (1-2000). If omitted, the coordinator falls back to its default page limit.
page_limit.title: Page Limit

* ``flow_ids``: an ordered list of flow ids. The server assigns

SegmentCondition.description:
Schema for a single segment condition.

Used in dynamic lists to filter contacts based on field values.

**Available filter fields:**

- ``contact_method``: Unified contact-method filter evaluated against the
  ``contact_methods`` table. Parameters:

  - ``method_type`` (required): one of ``whatsapp_id``, ``telegram_id``,
    ``email``, ``phone``, ``messenger_id``, ``instagram_id``.
  - ``operator``: ``has`` / ``not_has`` (presence checks), or ``equals`` /
    ``contains`` (value matches, requires ``value``).
  - ``value``: string to match (only for ``equals`` / ``contains``).
  - ``channel_id`` (optional UUID): only meaningful for the page-scoped
    types ``messenger_id`` / ``instagram_id``; ignored for global types.
  - ``phone_type`` (optional, e.g. ``mobile``): only meaningful for
    ``phone``.

  Value matching normalizes the input the same way the write path does
  (digits-only for phone-shaped types, lowercase for email), so saved
  filters reliably match stored rows.
- ``name``: Contact name filter (operators: equals, contains).
- ``email``, ``phone``: Contact field filters (operators: equals, contains).
  These now evaluate against the ``contact_methods`` table (matching across
  all of a contact's methods, not just the denormalized primary), so a
  contact with a non-primary matching email/phone is now included.
- ``custom_field``: Custom field filter (requires ``key``; operators: equals, contains, gt, gte, lt, lte).
- ``has_tag`` / ``not_has_tag``: Tag membership (value = tag UUID).
- ``has_telegram``, ``has_whatsapp``, ``has_messenger``, ``has_instagram``:
  Retained legacy aliases for boolean channel-presence checks
  (operator: equals, value: true/false). Prefer ``contact_method`` with
  ``operator=has``/``not_has`` for new filters.
- ``has_optin``: Subscription/opt-in check via ``contact_subscriptions``.
  Extra parameters: ``list_id`` (optional UUID), ``channel_type`` (optional; any
  ``SubscriptionChannelType`` value — see the field description for the live list),
  ``require_confirmed`` (optional bool).
  When ``value`` is true, matches contacts WITH a matching subscription; when false, matches
  contacts WITHOUT one.
- ``not_has_optin``: Alias that negates ``has_optin`` (value=true means no subscription).

SendTemplateCardParams.description:
Per-card send parameters for a CAROUSEL template.

Supplied positionally in ``SendTemplateRequest.cards`` — index 0 fills the
first card, index 1 the second, and so on. Each card's ``variable_values``
follows the SAME positional/named rules (and reserved-key handling) as the
top-level body ``variable_values``, resolved against that card's own body
placeholders. This is the template-send INPUT shape; the service maps it
onto the unified carousel content representation before dispatch.

header_media_url.description: Header media reference for THIS card's IMAGE/VIDEO header. Accepts the same forms as the top-level `header_media_url` (bare attachment id, proxy URL, permanent public URL, legacy GCS URL, or an external https URL). Each carousel card has its own header media, so supply one per card.
header_media_url.title: Header Media Url

variable_values.description: Values for this card's body placeholders. Same shape rules as the top-level `variable_values`: a list (positional only) or a dict (numeric keys for positional, identifier keys for named). Must match the template's `parameter_format`. Reserved dict keys (`url_suffix`, `otp_code`, and their indexed variants) apply per card.
variable_values.title: Variable Values

SendTemplateCardParams.title: SendTemplateCardParams

SendTemplateRequest.description:
Request to send a template message.

``variable_values`` accepts EITHER a list (positional templates) OR a dict
(positional with numeric keys, or named with identifier keys). The accepted
shape is determined by the template's ``parameter_format``:

* ``positional`` template → ``["John", "ORD-98765"]`` or
  ``{"1": "John", "2": "ORD-98765"}``.
* ``named`` template → ``{"first_name": "John", "order_id": "ORD-98765"}``.

Sending the wrong shape returns 400 with an actionable error. Order in the
NAMED dict is irrelevant — Meta resolves by ``parameter_name``.

Reserved keys in ``variable_values`` (only valid when passed as a dict;
they coexist with the regular body variable keys ``"1"``, ``"2"``, ... or
named identifiers):

* ``url_suffix`` — replaces the ``{{1}}`` placeholder inside a dynamic URL
  button (e.g. template URL ``https://example.com/orders/{{1}}``). Pass
  ONLY the suffix portion that fills ``{{1}}``, not the full URL. This
  key targets button index 0; use the indexed form below to address
  additional dynamic URL buttons on the same template.
* ``url_suffix_<button_index>`` — same as ``url_suffix`` but addresses a
  specific button by its 0-based index in the template's ``BUTTONS``
  component (e.g. ``url_suffix_1`` for the second button). When both
  ``url_suffix`` and ``url_suffix_0`` are present, the indexed form wins.
* ``otp_code`` — the code value for an authentication / OTP COPY_CODE
  button. This is the string the user copies when tapping the button.
* ``otp_code_<button_index>`` — indexed variant for templates with more
  than one COPY_CODE button. Same precedence rules as ``url_suffix_*``.

cards.description: Per-card parameters for a CAROUSEL template, supplied POSITIONALLY — entry 0 fills the first card, entry 1 the second, etc. Provide one entry per card you want to personalize. When ABSENT the non-carousel send path is unchanged. Each entry carries its own `variable_values` (same positional/named rules as the top-level field) and `header_media_url`. Only meaningful for CAROUSEL templates; ignored otherwise.
cards.title: Cards

channel_id.description: OPTIONAL. A WhatsApp channel id (UUID) owned by the tenant. Always allowed alongside any recipient selector. Used to (a) disambiguate a template referenced by NAME that exists on multiple channels, and (b) select the sending channel when sending by `whatsapp_id` with no contact/conversation. If it conflicts with the resolved template's own channel, the request returns 400.
channel_id.title: Channel Id

contact_id.description: Contact to send the message to. OPTIONAL — supply ANY ONE of `contact_id`, `contact_method_id`, `conversation_id`, or `whatsapp_id` to identify the recipient. If `contact_method_id` is also provided it WINS and this `contact_id` is ignored. When combined with `whatsapp_id`, this contact is used (and a matching WhatsApp contact method is auto-created on it if missing).
contact_id.title: Contact Id

contact_method_id.description: OPTIONAL. A `contact_methods.id` (UUID) of type `whatsapp_id` or `whatsapp_bsuid` owned by the tenant. When provided it determines BOTH the recipient WhatsApp id (the method's value) AND the contact (the method's owning contact). Highest-priority recipient selector — if both `contact_id` and `contact_method_id` are given, `contact_method_id` WINS and `contact_id` is ignored. A method of any other type returns 422.
contact_method_id.title: Contact Method Id

conversation_id.description: Link to existing conversation (creates new if not provided)
conversation_id.title: Conversation Id

header_document_filename.description: Optional filename override for DOCUMENT-type template headers. Must include the correct file extension matching the document (e.g. 'invoice.pdf' for a PDF). Ignored for non-DOCUMENT headers.
header_document_filename.title: Header Document Filename

header_media_url.description:
Header media reference for IMAGE/VIDEO/DOCUMENT templates. Accepts ANY of:
- a bare `attachment_id` (UUID) returned by `POST /attachments` or `POST /whatsapp-templates/upload-media`
- the proxy URL `/api/v1/attachments/{id}/download` (relative or absolute)
- the permanent public URL `/api/v1/attachments/public/{tenant_id}/{id}`
- a legacy `https://storage.googleapis.com/...` GCS URL
- any absolute external `https://` URL (customer CDN, etc.)

The server resolves the input to a Meta-deliverable URL via `WhatsAppHeaderMediaService`. Field name is kept for backwards compatibility — it has not been URL-only since May 2026.
header_media_url.title: Header Media Url

language.description:
OPTIONAL. Template language to send when the template is referenced BY NAME and that name exists in multiple languages. Use the exact code stored in `whatsapp_templates.language` — the Meta language/locale code (e.g. `en`, `de`, `en_US`, `pt_BR`).

Resolution when a name maps to multiple language rows (after the channel filter): if only one language remains it is used; if several remain, an explicit `language` selects that variant (400 if no such variant), else the recipient contact's stored `language` is matched (exact, then base-language family e.g. `de_DE`↔`de`), else 400 asking for `language`. When the template is referenced by DB ID the language is fixed by that row; passing a conflicting `language` returns 400.
language.title: Language

variable_values.description:
Override auto-mapped values. Pass a list (positional only) or a dict (positional with numeric keys, or named with identifier keys). Shape must match the template's parameter_format.

Reserved dict keys (coexist with body variable keys):
- `url_suffix` — replaces `{{1}}` inside a dynamic URL button. Value is ONLY the suffix portion that fills `{{1}}`, not the full URL (e.g. for template URL `https://example.com/orders/{{1}}`, pass `"url_suffix": "track/INV-2026-001"`).
- `otp_code` — the code copied by the user for authentication / OTP COPY_CODE buttons.
variable_values.title: Variable Values

whatsapp_id.description: OPTIONAL. A WhatsApp recipient id sent directly — a phone number WITHOUT a leading `+` (a leading `+` is stripped; spaces/dashes/parens are tolerated for phone-shaped values), an alphanumeric WhatsApp id (Meta now permits alphanumeric ids — digits are NOT required), OR a Business-scoped user ID such as `US.13491208655302741918` (kept verbatim, periods included, and sent in Meta's `recipient` field instead of `to`). The value is normalized with the same canonical contact-method normalization used elsewhere so dedup is consistent. If `contact_id` is also supplied, that contact gains a `whatsapp_id` (or `whatsapp_bsuid`) method with this value (created if missing); otherwise an existing contact is matched by this identifier, or a new contact + method is created. Note that AUTHENTICATION templates cannot be sent to a Business-scoped user ID (Meta error 131062). When sent without a `conversation_id`, the new conversation's channel is the template's channel (optionally selected via `channel_id`).

Sourced from the `email_messages` table (support replies, 1:1 sends) --
the same source billing invoices as MESSAGE_EMAIL. `sent` counts rows in
a billable status (sent or delivered); email has no billable 'read' state.

SmsPricelistResponse.description:
Full SMS pricelist — every country with per-segment fees.

``supported_countries`` is the canonical list of ISO-2 codes where
SendSeven currently offers SMS sending; client code can rely on this
instead of filtering rows by ``is_supported``.
SmsPricelistResponse.title: SmsPricelistResponse

SmsSenderResponse.description:
One configured SMS sender.

**SECURITY — hand-whitelisted projection.** ``ChannelResponse`` in
``app/schemas/channel.py`` deliberately excludes ``Channel.config``
because it holds API tokens, secrets and credentials that must NEVER be
returned via the API. This schema exists so the frontend can see the few
non-secret SMS facts it needs (``sender_type``, ``mode``,
``msisdn_or_alpha``) WITHOUT that ban being relaxed. Every field below is
named explicitly — the endpoint never dumps ``config``, and in particular
never exposes ``seven_io_subaccount_id``. Do not add a passthrough field.

can_receive.description: True iff replies route back into a conversation. False for alphanumeric and for shared_pool in send_only mode.
can_receive.title: Can Receive

channel_id.description: Channel UUID
channel_id.title: Channel Id

inbound_sms_rate_eur.description: The tenant's per-SMS rate in EUR from their pricing model (cost_message_sms, falling back to cost_message). Populated only when can_receive is true — a routed inbound reply is billed as an ordinary SMS at this rate, NOT as a separate surcharge. null when the sender cannot receive or the rate cannot be resolved.
inbound_sms_rate_eur.title: Inbound Sms Rate Eur

is_default_for_send.description: True for the ONE sender an auto-selected send will use (see SMS_SENDER_PRIORITY in app/services/sms/sender_identity.py). Never true for an inactive sender.
is_default_for_send.title: Is Default For Send

mode.description: Operating mode. Legacy rows without config.mode default to send_and_receive; alphanumeric senders are always send_only.
mode.title: Mode

msisdn_or_alpha.description: The MSISDN or alphanumeric sender id. null for shared_pool — seven.io picks a pool number per send.
msisdn_or_alpha.title: Msisdn Or Alpha

SmsSenderResponse.title: SmsSenderResponse

SnoozeConversationRequest.description:
Request body for snoozing (postponing) a conversation.

Snooze is a derived state: the conversation status remains ``open`` while
snoozed; it is hidden from the Open tab and surfaced on the Snoozed tab
until ``snoozed_until`` passes (query-time expiry, no background job).

reopen_on_message.description: When true, an inbound customer message arriving while the conversation is snoozed clears the snooze and returns it to the Open tab (handled by the inbound-message worker).
reopen_on_message.title: Reopen On Message

snoozed_until.description: Timezone-aware ISO datetime when the snooze should expire. Must be in the future. After this moment the conversation behaves as a normal open conversation again.
snoozed_until.title: Snoozed Until

SocialCommentResponse.description:
One comment plus everything the UI needs to render its row.

Deliberately answers three questions a list row has to answer on its own:
*what was said*, *what state is it in*, and *can I still privately reply —
and if not, why not*.

attachment_type.description: Kind of `attachment_url`: `image` (photos and stickers) or `video`. Null when the comment has no media.
attachment_type.title: Attachment Type

attachment_url.description: URL of the comment's media, for a photo/sticker/video comment (these carry no text). A Facebook feature — Instagram comments cannot contain media. May be a signed CDN URL that expires.
attachment_url.title: Attachment Url

author_external_id.description: The commenter's platform-scoped id (Instagram IGSID / Facebook PSID).
author_external_id.title: Author External Id

author_username.description: The commenter's username/handle, when Meta supplied one.
author_username.title: Author Username

channel_id.description: Channel the post belongs to.
channel_id.title: Channel Id

commented_at.description: Meta's timestamp for the comment — the business time.
commented_at.title: Commented At

contact_id.description: The commenter as a contact in your workspace. Null until they are resolved — which happens the first time we message them.
contact_id.title: Contact Id

external_comment_id.description: Meta's comment id. **This is the value to pass to `POST /comments/{comment_id}/private-reply`**, and the value that appears on the reply message as `meta.comment_id`.
external_comment_id.title: External Comment Id

handled_at.description: When the comment was marked handled or ignored.
handled_at.title: Handled At

is_from_owner.description: True when the comment is from the connected account itself — most often our own public reply, which Meta echoes back as an ordinary comment. Such comments never count as unanswered and are hidden from listings unless `include_owner=true`.
is_from_owner.title: Is From Owner

is_reply.description: True when this comment is a threaded reply to another comment (`parent_external_comment_id` is set).
is_reply.title: Is Reply

parent_external_comment_id.description: Meta's id of the comment this one replies to. Null for a top-level comment.
parent_external_comment_id.title: Parent External Comment Id

post.description: The post this comment was left on. Included where the caller has no post context (the cross-post inbox, and a single comment); omitted from the per-post thread, where it would repeat.

private_reply.description: The reply message itself, hydrated for rendering. Omitted when `include_reply=false`, and null when the message row is gone — message retention can outrun comment retention, and the comment must keep saying it WAS answered.

private_reply_available.description: Whether a private reply can still be sent right now. **False is the normal end state of most comments**, not an error — see `private_reply_unavailable_reason` for which one applies.
private_reply_available.title: Private Reply Available

private_reply_message_id.description: `messages.id` of the private reply that answered this comment — the link from a comment to its reply. Set for a reply we sent ourselves; null for a flow hand-off, where the flow's Send node owns the outbound message.
private_reply_message_id.title: Private Reply Message Id

private_reply_unavailable_reason.description:
Why `private_reply_available` is false, so the UI can say it rather than just grey out a button:

* `already_replied` — a private reply was already sent. Meta permits exactly one per comment, **forever**. Permanent.
* `window_expired` — the 7-day window closed. Permanent.
* `window_unknown` — Meta gave no reliable comment timestamp, so we cannot prove the window is open; we fail closed rather than offer a reply that Meta would reject.
* `marked_handled` — an agent cleared it without replying. Reversible: reopen it with `PATCH /comments/{comment_id}`.
* `ignored` — our own comment, or dismissed by a rule. Also reversible.

Null when a private reply IS available.
private_reply_unavailable_reason.title: Private Reply Unavailable Reason

private_reply_window_expires_at.description: End of Meta's 7-day private-reply window, measured from `commented_at`. Null when Meta gave no reliable comment timestamp.
private_reply_window_expires_at.title: Private Reply Window Expires At

public_reply_id.description: Meta's comment id of our public reply, when one was posted. Reserved: public replies are not part of the current release.
public_reply_id.title: Public Reply Id

replied_at.description: When the private reply was sent.
replied_at.title: Replied At

replied_by_user_id.description: The agent who replied, or who marked the comment handled. Null for an automated reply and for API-token callers.
replied_by_user_id.title: Replied By User Id

social_post_id.description: Our id for the post it was left on.
social_post_id.title: Social Post Id

state.description: `pending` (unanswered) · `auto_replied` (a rule or flow answered it) · `replied` (an agent answered it) · `handled` (cleared without a private reply) · `ignored` (our own comment, or dismissed).
state.title: State

text.description: The comment text. Null for a media-only comment.
text.title: Text

updated_at.description: When the resource was last updated (UTC)
updated_at.title: Updated At

SocialCommentResponse.title: SocialCommentResponse

SocialCommentRuleAction.description:
What a matching rule does. Exactly two options, on purpose.

``send_private_reply`` — the 90% case: one static (variable-substituted)
DM. Text-only, because Meta's private-reply API is text-only.

``start_flow`` — the escape hatch for "one entry message, then wait for the
user's answer". Hands off to the existing flow engine rather than growing a
second conversation runtime inside the rules engine.
SocialCommentRuleAction.title: SocialCommentRuleAction

SocialCommentRuleButton.description:
One button on a rule's private reply.

Shape-only validation lives here (enum membership, lengths). Everything
needing the database or the channel — "is this an Instagram channel?",
"does this flow exist in this tenant and can it be started from a button?"
— is enforced by ``private_reply_buttons.validate_and_normalize_buttons``
in the service layer, which is the SAME validator the manual
``POST /comments/{id}/private-reply`` endpoint runs. There is exactly one
set of button rules in the product.

action.description: What a `postback` button does. `start_flow` starts `flow_id` for the person who tapped. Implied when `flow_id` is set.
action.title: Action

attachment_id.description: Editor-side hint on a `url` button whose URL is an attachment's public link ("file button"). Stored so the editor can re-open the button as a file; never sent to the recipient. The link is not reference-counted — deleting the attachment later breaks it.
attachment_id.title: Attachment Id

flow_id.description: Flow started by a `start_flow` button. Must be published and in this workspace, and must NOT be a "Comment received" flow — that trigger is reserved for the first message, whose one allowed private reply is the message carrying this button.
flow_id.title: Flow Id

payload.description: Opaque value returned to you on tap (as `meta.button_id`). Defaults to the label. Mutually exclusive with `action`/`flow_id`.
payload.title: Payload

source.description: Editor-side hint naming where a `url` button's link came from (e.g. `attachment`). Stored, never sent to the recipient.
source.title: Source

type.description: `url` opens a link; `postback` sends a value back to you.
type.title: Type

url.description: Destination of a `url` button. Absolute **https** URL, required for that type and rejected on a `postback` button.
url.title: Url

SocialCommentRuleButton.title: SocialCommentRuleButton

SocialCommentRuleCreate.description: POST body. ``channel_id`` is immutable, so it only exists here.

action.description: Send a private reply, or hand the comment off to a flow.

channel_id.description: The Instagram or Facebook channel this rule watches.
channel_id.title: Channel Id

enabled.description: Disabled rules are skipped entirely during evaluation.
enabled.title: Enabled

flow_id.description: Flow to start when action is start_flow. The flow's trigger must be "Comment received".
flow_id.title: Flow Id

keywords.description: Keywords to match. Ignored when match_mode is any_comment.
keywords.title: Keywords

match_mode.description: any_comment reacts to every comment (no keywords needed, and it also matches comments with no text at all). contains / exact / starts_with compare against the keyword list, case-insensitively.

name.description: Operator-facing label, e.g. "Summer sale — send the code".
name.title: Name

post_ids.description: Post identifiers to watch when post_scope is specific_posts. These are the platform's own post ids as returned by the channel's posts/media listing endpoint.
post_ids.title: Post Ids

post_message_overrides.description: Optional per-post wording: {post_id: message}. A post listed here gets that message instead of reply_text; every other post falls back to reply_text.
post_message_overrides.title: Post Message Overrides

post_scope.description: Watch every post on the channel, or only selected posts.

priority.description: Evaluation order — LOWER runs FIRST (same convention as flows). The first matching rule wins; no further rule is evaluated. Ties are broken by specificity (a post-scoped, keyworded rule beats a catch-all), then by age.
priority.title: Priority

reply_buttons.description: Up to 3 buttons attached to the private reply. Supported on both Facebook Messenger and Instagram. A control the rule's channel cannot carry is rejected when the rule is saved, not silently stripped when it fires. Only meaningful when action is send_private_reply.
reply_buttons.title: Reply Buttons

reply_quick_replies.description: DEPRECATED / IGNORED. Comment private replies are buttons-only since 2026-08-13. This field is still accepted for backwards compatibility so older clients do not get a 422, but it is never validated, stored, or sent — use reply_buttons instead.
reply_quick_replies.title: Reply Quick Replies

reply_text.description: The private reply to send. Supports the same {{placeholders}} as the flow Send node — for example {{contact.first_name}} — plus {{comment.text}}, {{comment.author}} and {{post.caption}}.
reply_text.title: Reply Text

SocialCommentRuleCreate.title: SocialCommentRuleCreate

SocialCommentRuleMatchMode.description:
How ``keywords`` are compared against the comment text.

``contains`` / ``exact`` / ``starts_with`` are the EXACT modes
``match_comment_trigger`` already implements (case-insensitive, trimmed).
``any_comment`` is the "reply to everything" option: it needs no keywords
and matches even a text-less (image / sticker) comment.
SocialCommentRuleMatchMode.title: SocialCommentRuleMatchMode

SocialCommentRulePostScope.description:
Which posts a rule watches. Stored LOWERCASE (values_callable).

Values are IDENTICAL to the ``scope`` values of the ``comment_received``
flow trigger config so a rule can be handed to ``match_comment_trigger``
verbatim.
SocialCommentRulePostScope.title: SocialCommentRulePostScope

SocialCommentRuleQuickReply.description:
One quick-reply chip on a rule's private reply.

The sibling of :class:`SocialCommentRuleButton`, and the same division of
labour: shape-only validation here, everything needing the database or the
channel in ``private_reply_buttons.validate_and_normalize_quick_replies``
— the SAME validator the manual endpoint runs.

Differs from a button exactly where Meta differs: 13 permitted instead of
3, a `content_type` instead of a `type`, and **no URL kind** (Meta's quick
reply object has no URL variant). A chip that starts a flow behaves
identically to a button that starts a flow, including the ban on
"Comment received" flows.

action.description: What the chip does. `start_flow` starts `flow_id` for the person who tapped. Implied when `flow_id` is set.
action.title: Action

content_type.description: Meta's chip kind. Only `text` is supported; the field exists so Meta's own documented payload validates unchanged.
content_type.title: Content Type

flow_id.description: Flow started by a `start_flow` chip. Must be published and in this workspace, and must NOT be a "Comment received" flow — that trigger is reserved for the first message, whose one allowed private reply is the message carrying this chip.
flow_id.title: Flow Id

payload.description: Opaque value returned to you on tap (as `meta.button_id`). Defaults to the label. Mutually exclusive with `action`/`flow_id`.
payload.title: Payload

title.description: Chip label (Meta limit: 20 characters, truncated beyond that).
title.title: Title

SocialCommentRuleQuickReply.title: SocialCommentRuleQuickReply

SocialCommentRuleUpdate.description:
PATCH body — every field optional.

Deliberately NOT a subclass of the base: inheriting would drag the base's
defaults in, and a default is indistinguishable from an omitted field in a
PATCH. Here, "absent" genuinely means "leave it alone" (the endpoint uses
``exclude_unset``), so a caller can toggle ``enabled`` without restating the
rule. ``channel_id`` is absent on purpose: moving a rule to another channel
silently changes which posts it can match, so that is a delete + create.
SocialCommentRuleUpdate.title: SocialCommentRuleUpdate

SocialCommentTriageRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /comments/{comment_id}` — clear a comment by hand.

state.description:
The new state:

* `handled` — you answered publicly or off-platform. Clears it from the unanswered queue.
* `ignored` — not actionable; skip it.
* `pending` — reopen a comment that was marked handled or ignored by mistake.

`replied` and `auto_replied` are **not** settable here: they mean a private reply message exists, and are set by actually sending one.
state.title: State

SocialCommentTriageRequest.title: SocialCommentTriageRequest

SocialInsightsMetrics.description:
Platform-agnostic metric snapshot. A `null` field means the platform (or
this object type) does NOT expose that metric — it is never fabricated.

Instagram media exposes reach + engagement (`total_interactions`) + likes /
comments / shares / saves, but NOT `impressions` on the current API. A
Facebook post/page exposes reach + impressions + engagement via `/insights`;
per-post likes/comments/shares come from a different edge and stay `null` in
Phase 1.
SocialInsightsMetrics.title: SocialInsightsMetrics

SocialInsightsTarget.description: Insights for one published target (one channel) of an authored post.

authorized.description: False when the connection lacks the insights permission — the frontend should prompt a reconnect. See `error_code`.
authorized.title: Authorized

channel_id.description: The channel this target published to.
channel_id.title: Channel Id

error_code.description: `insights_not_authorized` (reconnect to grant insights), `insights_unavailable` (Meta has no insights for this object), `insights_unsupported_platform`, or `insights_error`. Null on success.
error_code.title: Error Code

last_refreshed_at.description: When this target's cached numbers were last refreshed from Meta. Null if this target has never been cached.
last_refreshed_at.title: Last Refreshed At

object_id.description: Meta's id read (IG media id / FB `{page}_{post}`).
object_id.title: Object Id

SocialInsightsTarget.title: SocialInsightsTarget

SocialPostInsights.description:
Cached Meta insights for one comment-synced post (the Posts-LIST view).

FLAT by design: the Posts list renders each metric as its own cell, so the
nine metrics sit at the top level rather than under a nested ``metrics``
object (this differs from the authored-post ``SocialInsightsTarget`` in
``schemas/social_post.py``, which groups them under ``metrics``). Every
metric is ``int | null`` — ``null`` means Meta (or this object type) does
not expose that metric, or it has not been fetched yet; a metric is never
fabricated from a different one.

Served from the ``social_posts.insights_*`` cache columns — the LIST endpoint
makes NO live Graph call on load. ``likes`` / ``comments`` fall back to the
post's public counters (``like_count`` / ``comments_count``) when the richer
insights value has not been cached yet, so the list shows a number before the
first insights refresh; a refreshed insights value always wins over the
public counter.

authorized.description: False when the connection lacks the insights permission — the frontend should prompt a reconnect. See `error_code`.
authorized.title: Authorized

error_code.description: `insights_not_authorized` (reconnect to grant insights), `insights_unavailable` (Meta has no insights for this object), `insights_unsupported_platform` (channel is not IG/FB), or `insights_error`. Null on success / before any refresh.
error_code.title: Error Code

last_refreshed_at.description: When these numbers were last refreshed from Meta. Null if this post's insights have never been refreshed (metrics are then null except the public-counter fallback for likes/comments).
last_refreshed_at.title: Last Refreshed At

SocialPostInsights.title: SocialPostInsights

SocialPostInsightsBulkRefreshResponse.description:
`POST /comments/posts/insights/refresh` — bulk refresh outcome.

Refreshes the tenant's most-recent posts (bounded by ``limit``) to avoid a
Graph storm, and returns each refreshed post with its updated insights.

items.description: One entry per refreshed post, most recent first.
items.title: Items

SocialPostInsightsBulkRefreshResponse.title: SocialPostInsightsBulkRefreshResponse

insights.description: The freshly-refreshed (and re-cached) insights for the post.

SocialPostInsightsSummaryResponse.description:
`GET /comments/posts/insights/summary` — aggregate insights totals.

Totals across the tenant's comment-synced posts, for two windows. The
30-day window sums posts published (``posted_at``) in the last 30 days; the
all-time window sums every non-deleted post. Because per-post insights are
Meta LIFETIME totals, the window selects WHICH posts are summed, not a daily
series.

last_refreshed_at.description: The most recent ``insights_refreshed_at`` across the tenant's posts — how fresh the freshest number in this summary is. Null when no post has ever been refreshed.
last_refreshed_at.title: Last Refreshed At

SocialPostInsightsSummaryResponse.title: SocialPostInsightsSummaryResponse

SocialPostInsightsWindow.description:
Summed insights across a set of comment-synced posts (one time window).

Per-post insights are Meta LIFETIME totals, so a window filters WHICH posts
are summed, NOT a per-day series — the totals are lifetime numbers for the
posts in scope. Each metric sums only the non-null cached values (so a metric
a platform never exposes never distorts the total); a metric is null only
when NO post in scope has a value for it. ``post_count`` is how many posts
have cached insights and thus contributed.

post_count.description: Posts in this window that have cached insights (``insights_refreshed_at`` set) and therefore contributed to the totals above.
post_count.title: Post Count

counters_synced_at.description: Last time the two counters were recomputed from the comment rows. Null means they have only ever been maintained incrementally.

like_count.description: Total reactions Meta reports on the post (all reaction types on Facebook, likes on Instagram). **Nullable** — null until the post has been read from Meta, and it can lag reality between syncs. This is Meta's public number, not derived from anything we store.

page_avatar_url.description: Profile-picture URL of the connected Page / Instagram account (the post owner). **Nullable** — a Meta CDN URL that can expire, and null for channels connected before the avatar was captured or when Meta returned none. Fall back to initials/`page_name` when absent.

page_name.description: Display name of the connected Page / Instagram account this post belongs to — the **post owner**, i.e. YOUR connected account, not the commenter. Taken from the channel's name, falling back to a channel-type label ("Instagram" / "Facebook Page") when the channel has no set name.

permalink.description: Public URL of the post on Instagram / Facebook.

posted_at.description: When the post was published on Meta — not when we learned about it. Null for a post Meta gave no timestamp for; such posts sort last.

thumbnail_url.description: URL of the post's card image. Normally a **permanent** URL on our own domain: we mirror the image once, because Meta's own CDN URLs expire. Falls back to Meta's expiring CDN URL for a post whose image could not be mirrored (it had already expired, or the post has no image at all).

post.description:
Rate an AI answer 👍 / 👎 / ✗ (upsert — re-rating replaces).

``down`` and ``wrong`` REQUIRE ``reason_category``: a verdict with no
reason cannot drive the correction loop and only produces noise in the
score.

A KB correction is opened (and an analysis job enqueued) when:

* the verdict is ``wrong`` — always; or
* the verdict is ``down`` **and** it carries substantive text in
  ``comment`` and/or ``better_answer``.

A bare 👎 with no prose stays a cheap score signal and spawns no job.
``correction_opened`` / ``correction_id`` in the response tell the caller
which happened, so the UI can confirm it and link to the review queue.

Opening a correction never publishes anything by itself: a ``down``-born
correction is review-only even for tenants in ``kb_correction_mode=auto``.

Returns the recomputed scores of every FAQ entry the verdict touched, so
the UI can reflect the consequence immediately.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:write`

Fetch a public URL server-side and store it as an attachment.

Returns the same shape as ``POST /upload`` so the response is
interchangeable. Caller can then pass the returned ``id`` /
``attachment_id`` in ``MessageCreate.attachments``.

Per-tenant URL dedup: if this tenant already has an attachment
whose ``source_url`` matches the requested ``url`` exactly, that
row is returned without re-fetching or re-uploading. To force a
re-fetch, vary the URL (e.g. add ``?t=12345``).

Security:
    - ``http://`` / ``https://`` only — ``file://``, ``gopher://``,
      ``data://`` etc. rejected.
    - Hostname resolved up-front; rejected if any A/AAAA record
      falls into loopback, RFC1918, link-local (incl. cloud
      metadata 169.254.169.254), ULA, reserved, or multicast.
    - Bytes validated against the same magic-byte sniffer as
      ``/upload`` AND against a stricter MIME allowlist
      (``URL_FETCH_ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES``).
    - 50 MB hard cap; streaming cut-off enforced even if the
      server lies in ``Content-Length``.

**Required Scopes:** ``messages:create``

Upload a file attachment

Args:
    file: The file to upload
    message_id: Optional message ID to associate with

Returns:
    Attachment ID and metadata

Security:
    - Validates file extension against blocklist
    - Validates file magic bytes match claimed MIME type
    - Enforces file size limits

**🔐 Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

delete.description:
Delete an attachment

Permanently removes the ``attachments`` row **and** its stored blob. This
is irreversible. Attachments are re-usable and carry no foreign key back
to the messages that referenced them, so deleting one that a previously
sent message still points at is allowed and expected — the message keeps
its metadata, the media simply stops resolving.

Args:
    attachment_id: ID of the attachment

Returns:
    ``204 No Content`` on success. ``404`` when the attachment does not
    exist or belongs to another tenant. ``500`` when the row exists but
    the delete itself failed (e.g. the storage backend errored) — in that
    case the row is left intact so the call can be retried.

**Required Scopes:** `messages:delete`

Returns:
    - total_cost_eur: RAW usage cost in EUR (before the included pool)
    - recipient_count: Number of recipients
    - breakdown: Cost breakdown by channel ({count, cost})
    - warnings: List of warnings about variable costs
    - can_send: Whether campaign can be sent based on balance
    - balance_error: Error message if insufficient balance
    - current_balance_eur: Current balance in EUR

Included-pool fields (base_fee plans only; 0 / null on legacy
`minimum_commit` plans or plans with no included pool -- the UI gates the
pool UI on `included_messages_total > 0` and otherwise headlines
`total_cost_eur`):
    - included_messages_total: effective pooled allowance this month (int)
    - included_messages_used: pooled units already consumed this month (int)
    - included_messages_remaining: max(0, total - used) (int)
    - projected_sends: billable send units this campaign draws (int)
    - sends_covered_by_pool: min(projected_sends, remaining) (int)
    - sends_over_pool: max(0, projected_sends - remaining) (int)
    - payable_overage_eur: EUR actually payable for THIS campaign after the
      pool absorbs what it can (0.00 when fully covered; null when no pool
      applies -- use total_cost_eur). Excludes Meta/WhatsApp per-conversation
      template fees, which Meta bills separately.
    - fully_covered: bool, true when sends_over_pool == 0
    - pool_is_shared: bool, true when the pool is shared across the account
      (human wording is authored on the frontend for i18n)

RCS Newsletter (MAU) agents (only present when the campaign sends via one):
    - rcs_newsletter: {recipient_count, sendseven_fee_eur: 0.0, billing: "mau"}.
      These recipients carry NO per-message fee and draw NO pool units, so
      they are excluded from total_cost_eur / breakdown / projected_sends
      (recipient_count still includes them). Their only cost is the monthly
      active user price from the RCS balance -- see `GET /rcs-estimate`.
